content.content:
A draft's record is a registry-local object whose identity is its own generated draft handle. The handle is minted for the draft and written into the record as its key, so exactly one record exists per draft and the record is the thing that key picks out. That identity is not a node id, not a change id, and is not derived from either: the handle names the draft and means nothing outside the registry, while node and change ids are the graph's identities for the nodes it holds.

Everything else a record carries is a reference, not identity. A record names exactly one target node and exactly one edit: the node whose content the draft changes, and the edit the draft belongs to. It also carries the workspace that holds the draft, by name and path, because a draft is written in its own workspace and the node does not say which one — the several drafts of one node sit in different workspaces, so the node and the edit together still do not say which draft the record is. Those three are the whole of a record's references, and they name the parts of a draft, not the record. A node and an edit cannot be the key for the same reason: one node may be named by several records at once — competing alternatives within one edit, or a redraft while an earlier draft is still open — and one edit is named by the records of every node it touches. A key is one per record; a node and an edit are many per record, so neither distinguishes one record from another. The handle alone does, which is why the key is a handle and the rest are references.

For the same reason a record is not a node document. It is not the document `nodes/<id>.json`, it is not listed with the nodes and their edges, and it is not validated as a node: the schema checks the node document, and the record is not one. Nor is its identity a change id — it is not attributed to a change, because attribution runs through node id and the record has none. The registry keeps records under its own key and stays outside the node space the graph lists and attributes; a record is not a node the listing omits, it was never in that set.

An edit exists in the registry only as the label its records share. Because records are keyed by handle, there is no key under which an edit record could sit, and none for an edit state; and an edit that is only a label has no placement of its own — the records carrying one label, read together, are all there is to an edit in the registry.
content.rationale:
The record exists because a draft's state has to live outside the repository and outside the graph at once. The registry is the state directory's untracked work area, so what it holds is deccy's state and not repository content (ulqqklzk); a draft outlives the command that opened it and may be redrafted while an earlier draft is open, so the record must be durable and addressable there. The graph's identity cannot supply that address. A node's id is the id of the jj change that owns it, appearing in the filename and in edge targets and never in the document (xwyryumr); a node is the JSON document `nodes/<id>.json` carrying kind, content and its outgoing edges (kpovwvyw); and what counts as a valid node is the schema over that document (tksoxwpy). None of these reaches a registry entry: a record has no change, no file under `nodes/`, no edges, and no document shape for the schema to accept. So the record's identity has to be minted for it — a generated handle — and the node model can only supply references.

The reference shape comes from the draft model: a draft names exactly one node and the edit it belongs to, is written in its own workspace, and several drafts may name one node — within one edit as competing alternatives and across edits as a redraft (znskspqs). That is why the record carries exactly one node, one edit and one workspace, and equally why none of them is its key: by construction they are many per record. Recording places the named edits into the named node's change (rvyrosmp), so naming the target is required of the record while the change remains the node's identity. `log` lists the node set with its edges and settles no filtering (zqkqvlyo); the record is outside that set because it is outside the node model, not because a listing excludes it.

The record's state and lifetime, its base content, operation ordering and undo, drift, and the verb surface are separate commitments decided elsewhere. This node fixes only that the record's identity is registry-local and that everything else it carries is a reference.
